findings.title: Reject non-positive flusher process counts
findings.body: The CLI accepts any integer for `--flusher-processes`, but `or` turns an explicit `0` into the number of assigned shards, defeating the configured cap and potentially spawning one process per shard. A negative value remains negative, produces an empty process map, and then raises `KeyError` when assigning a shard, crashing the consumer. Validate that the value is positive before computing the process count.

findings.title: Terminate workers when the join deadline expires
findings.body: When the deadline has expired, this `break` skips the termination code for the current worker and every remaining worker. The deadline may already be consumed by `next_step.join(timeout)`, so a wedged flusher process can survive strategy shutdown with access to Redis and Kafka; later workers are also left running. Ensure timed-out workers are terminated rather than breaking out before cleanup.

findings.title: The process-limit test exercises threads, not processes
findings.body: Passing `produce_to_pipe` makes `SpanFlusher` choose `threading.Thread`, so this test's process-count assertions only verify the shard mapping and do not exercise the new spawn-process path. It will not catch failures in process startup, argument pickling, or process cleanup. Add coverage that starts the real multiprocessing branch (with Kafka production suitably mocked).
